title: Jailbreak Transfer as a Homogeneity Metric: Cheap Attacks on One Model, Tested on Many

original_idea.body:
# Jailbreak Transfer as a Homogeneity Metric: Cheap Attacks on One Model, Tested on Many

**Problem:** Jailbreak transferability tracks representation similarity, implying transfer rate is a behavioral measure of homogeneity. No one has used a fixed jailbreak suite as a lightweight cross-model homogeneity probe.

**Direction:** Replicate public jailbreak prompts across 8-10 open models, recording which break on which. Twist: build a shared-vulnerability matrix and correlate it with benign output-homogeneity.

**Why it matters:** If similar benign outputs predict shared jailbreak vulnerabilities, output-homogeneity becomes a cheap early-warning proxy.

**Relevant context:** Jailbreak Transferability Emerges from Shared Representations (arXiv:2506.12913); Zou et al. universal-suffix transfer.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: benign-homogeneity as a cheap early-warning proxy for shared exploitability targets a recognized robustness pathway with a defensible deliverable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Public jailbreaks plus a vulnerability matrix and correlation; accessible, no novel attacks.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused: shared-vulnerability matrix correlated with benign homogeneity; clear endpoint.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public jailbreaks/models, no lab access; defensive proxy of high external value.

novelty.reasoning: Using benign homogeneity to predict shared exploitability appears largely unmeasured.
